key_insight: UniSlider makes image-editing sliders behave more like humans expect: equal movements on the slider produce more evenly spaced perceptual changes in the edited image. Instead of tying the slider directly to an internal model strength, it remaps the control to better match visible change.
problem_solved: Current AI image-editing sliders are often poorly aligned with perception: some regions of the slider do almost nothing, while others cause sudden, abrupt changes. This paper addresses the mismatch between a model's numeric strength parameter and the user's visual experience of continuous editing.
method: Analyze how existing strength parameters translate into perceptual image change across the slider range.
Introduce a remapping strategy that redistributes slider positions so visual edits progress more uniformly.
Preserve intuitive continuous control while reducing dead zones, reversals, and sudden jumps in appearance.
impact: For practitioners, this improves the usability of generative editing tools by making sliders predictable, smooth, and easier to tune. It can reduce trial-and-error, improve user trust, and make interactive image editing workflows more efficient.

paper_title: UniSlider: Perceptually Uniform Sliders for Continuous Image Editing
paper_authors: David Serrano-Lozano, Duygu Ceylan, Yannick Hold-Geoffroy, Iliyan Georgiev, Javier Vazquez-Corral
